findings.claim: Loose documentation. (1) The docstring and the module docstring (L24) say 'a Jordan decomposition *of a measurable space*'; it is a pair of mutually singular finite measures *on* `α`, i.e. the Jordan decomposition of the signed measure `posPart - negPart`. (2) The module docstring says `j` decomposes `s` if `s = j.posPart - j.negPart`. In Lean that is `Measure`'s truncated subtraction, which for any Jordan decomposition equals `j.posPart` (proved below), so the literal formula is wrong. The intended `j.posPart.toSignedMeasure - j.negPart.toSignedMeasure` is `j.toSignedMeasure`. (3) The field docstrings lack full stops. (Astra's blind pass, item 3, independently flags the literal formula as misleading.)
findings.fix: Reword to 'a pair of mutually singular finite measures on `α`' and write `s = j.toSignedMeasure` (not `s = j.posPart - j.negPart`) in the module docstring, ending the field docstrings with full stops.
findings.ev:
-- hunts/vm-jordan/batch0/probe3.lean (compiles; imports JordanSub)
example (j : JordanDecomposition α) : j.posPart - j.negPart = j.posPart := by
  have h := Measure.toJordanDecomposition_toSignedMeasure_sub (μ := j.posPart) (ν := j.negPart)
  have h2 : (j.posPart.toSignedMeasure - j.negPart.toSignedMeasure).toJordanDecomposition = j :=
    JordanDecomposition.toJordanDecomposition_toSignedMeasure j
  rw [h2] at h
  exact (congrArg JordanDecomposition.posPart h).symm

findings.claim: Non-defeq instance diamond on `SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)`. Because the file also declares `instSMulReal : SMul ℝ (JordanDecomposition α)` (L91), Mathlib's generic `NNReal.instSMulOfReal : [SMul ℝ M] → SMul ℝ≥0 M` (Mathlib/Basic/NNReal/Defs.lean:258, `c • m := (c : ℝ) • m`) already provides an `SMul ℝ≥0` instance. With `instSMul` erased, `#synth SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)` returns `NNReal.instSMulOfReal`. The hand-written `instSMul` (`⟨r • j.posPart, r • j.negPart, _⟩`) is not defeq to it, at either reducible-and-instances or default transparency: the generic one unfolds to the classical `if 0 ≤ (r : ℝ) then … else …` of `instSMulReal`. The two agree only propositionally (`coe_smul`). `r • j` elaborates to `instSMul`, so generic lemmas stated for the derived instance do not fire. `NNReal.smul_def r j : r • j = (r : ℝ) • j` is rejected with a type mismatch that differs only in the instance, and `rw [NNReal.smul_def]` reports no occurrence of `?c • ?x` in `r • j = ↑r • j`. No open upstream PR (gh search 'JordanDecomposition smul', 'toJordanDecomposition', 'instSMulOfReal diamond'). Astra's targeted refutation (A2.answer.md) agrees it is a genuine non-defeq diamond on operation data but rates it MINOR: API/instance hygiene with an existing workaround (`coe_smul`), not a wrong statement or an exact duplicate definition; graded MINOR under the lane's calibration.
findings.fix: Delete `instSMul` so that `SMul ℝ≥0` is the inherited `NNReal.instSMulOfReal`, define `instSMulReal` through a plain `def nnsmul` scaling both parts, and reprove `smul_posPart`/`smul_negPart`/`real_smul_def`/`real_smul_nonneg`/`real_smul_neg` in one line each (`coe_smul` becomes `rfl`); the rest of the file compiles unchanged.
findings.ev:
-- hunts/vm-jordan/batch0/probe2.lean (output probe2.out), probe1.lean (probe1.out)
attribute [-instance] MeasureTheory.JordanDecomposition.instSMul in
#synth SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)   -- NNReal.instSMulOfReal
example : (instSMul : SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)) = NNReal.instSMulOfReal := by
  with_reducible_and_instances rfl   -- error: not definitionally equal
example : (instSMul : SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)) = NNReal.instSMulOfReal := by
  rfl                                -- error: not definitionally equal
-- propositionally equal (compiles):
example : (instSMul : SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)) = NNReal.instSMulOfReal := by
  have e1 : (instSMul : SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)) = ⟨fun r j => instSMul.smul r j⟩ := rfl
  have e2 : (NNReal.instSMulOfReal : SMul ℝ≥0 (JordanDecomposition α)) =
      ⟨fun r j => NNReal.instSMulOfReal.smul r j⟩ := rfl
  rw [e1, e2]; congr 1; funext r j; exact (coe_smul j r).symm
-- consequence (both fail):
example (r : ℝ≥0) (j : JordanDecomposition α) : r • j = (r : ℝ) • j := NNReal.smul_def r j  -- Type mismatch (instSMulOfReal vs instSMul)
example (r : ℝ≥0) (j : JordanDecomposition α) : r • j = (r : ℝ) • j := by rw [NNReal.smul_def]  -- did not find ?c • ?x
-- fix verified: hunts/vm-jordan/batch0/fixed_diamond.lean (src.lean minus instSMul, plus `nnsmul`) compiles with no errors or warnings (fixed_diamond.out empty)

findings.claim: `VectorMeasure.AbsolutelyContinuous v w` is `∀ s, w s = 0 → v s = 0`. For a nonnegative reference measure this is the usual notion, but the definition accepts any vector measure `w`, and for signed `w` cancellation makes it a different, stronger relation than absolute continuity (`|w|`-null sets are `v`-null). With `w = δ_true − δ_false` and `v = δ_true` on `Bool`: `¬ v ≪ᵥ w` (as `w univ = 0`, `v univ = 1`), although `v` vanishes on every `w`-null set; and `v = w.restrict {true}`, so even a restriction of `w` is not `≪ᵥ w`. Graded MINOR, not MAJOR/CRITICAL: every use of `≪ᵥ` in Mathlib (RadonNikodym, WithDensity, Jordan, Complex, Variation) has an `ℝ≥0∞` reference measure, where the definition is standard, so no stated theorem is false. Flagged to the user as a candidate for escalation.
findings.fix: Either document that for signed/vector-valued `w` this is the zero-set relation (not absolute continuity), or restrict `w` to `VectorMeasure α ℝ≥0∞` / define via `w.ennrealVariation`.

findings.ev:
theorem le_variation_noMeas (μ : VectorMeasure X V) {s : Set X} {P : Finset (Set X)}
    (hP₁ : ∀ t ∈ P, t ⊆ s) (hP₂ : (P : Set (Set X)).PairwiseDisjoint id) :
    ∑ p ∈ P, ‖μ p‖ₑ ≤ μ.variation s :=
  (μ.le_variation (measurableSet_toMeasurable _ s)
    (fun t ht => (hP₁ t ht).trans (subset_toMeasurable _ _)) hP₂).trans_eq (measure_toMeasurable s)

example (μ : VectorMeasure X V) (E : Set X) : ‖μ E‖ₑ ≤ μ.variation E := by
  simpa using μ.le_variation_noMeas (P := {E}) (by simp) (by simp)

    {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : 0 < ε) (hμ : μ.variation s ≠ ∞) :
    ∃ (P : Finset (Set X)), (∀ t ∈ P, t ⊆ s) ∧ ((P : Set (Set X)).PairwiseDisjoint id) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ P, MeasurableSet t) ∧ μ.variation s ≤ ∑ p ∈ P, ‖μ p‖ₑ + ε := by
  rcases eq_or_ne (μ.variation s) 0 with h0 | h0
  · exact ⟨∅, by simp [h0]⟩
  obtain ⟨P, h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄⟩ :=
    μ.exists_lt_sum_of_lt_variation hs (ENNReal.sub_lt_self hμ h0 hε.ne')
  exact ⟨P, h₁, h₂, h₃, tsub_le_iff_right.1 h₄.le⟩

findings.claim: The proof spends 7 lines (a nested `have` using `variation_apply_eq_zero`, `measure_union` and two `grind` calls) proving the equality `(μ.map φ).variation s = (μ.map φ).variation (s ∩ range φ)`, but only `≥` is used, and that is `measure_mono inter_subset_left`; dropping the detour shortens the proof from 15 to 8 lines.

findings.ev:
In hunts/vm-variation/batch1/src_edit.lean (whole file compiles with Mathlib's options, no warnings):
theorem _root_.MeasurableEmbedding.variation_map (hφ : MeasurableEmbedding φ) :
    (μ.map φ).variation = μ.variation.map φ := by
  refine le_antisymm variation_map_le (Measure.le_iff.2 fun s hs ↦ ?_)
  rw [hφ.map_apply]
  grw [← measure_mono (μ := (μ.map φ).variation) (inter_subset_left (t := range φ)),
    ← hφ.comap_preimage]
  refine Measure.le_iff'.1 (variation_le_of_forall_enorm_le fun t ht ↦ ?_) _
  rw [hφ.comap_apply]
  refine le_of_eq_of_le ?_ (enorm_measure_le_variation _ _)
  rw [map_apply _ hφ.measurable (hφ.measurableSet_image.2 ht), preimage_image_eq _ hφ.injective]
(a calc version is in probe1.lean P3)

findings.claim: The private `variation_smul_le` assumes `[NormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V]`, but the inequality holds for any `[SeminormedRing R] [Module R V] [IsBoundedSMul R V]`, where the equality `variation_smul` fails. For example, with componentwise multiplication on ℝ×ℝ, c = (1,0) and μ = dirac x (0,1), the left side is 0 and the right side is 1. As the `norm_smul_le` analogue it should be public. The finite-variation instance at L333 is stated with the same field assumptions, so it misses normed-ring scalars. For `A` a `NormedRing`, `IsFiniteMeasure (c • μ).variation` for `μ : VectorMeasure X A`, `c : A` is not found, and it follows at once from the generalised lemma via `isFiniteMeasure_of_le`.
findings.fix: Make `variation_smul_le` public over `[SeminormedRing R] [Module R V] [IsBoundedSMul R V]` (proof: add `enorm_smul_le` to the `grw`) and derive the L333 instance as `isFiniteMeasure_of_le _ variation_smul_le` under the same assumptions.

findings.claim: `variation_smul` assumes `[NormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V]`, but the equality holds for any `[SeminormedRing R] [Module R V] [NormSMulClass R V]`. A direct proof (pull `‖c‖ₑ` out of each partition sum, then `ENNReal.mul_iSup`) needs no inverse, and in the `ENormedAddCommMonoid` setting gives `(c • μ).variation = ‖c‖ₑ • μ.variation` for any `[ENormSMulClass R V]`. Natural cases the current statement misses: quaternion scalars (`ℍ` is a `NormedDivisionRing`, not a `NormedField`) and `ℝ≥0`-scaling of `ℝ≥0∞`-valued vector measures. The 10-line inverse-trick proof and its private helper become unnecessary.

findings.claim: `IsSemiprime` is introduced but no declaration mentions it: there is no characterisation `IsSemiprime n ↔ ∃ p q, p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ n = p * q` (provable in six lines from `List.length_eq_two`, `Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList`, `Nat.prod_primeFactorsList`), and the constructors `Prime.mul_isAlmostPrime_two` / `sq_isAlmostPrime_two` state `IsAlmostPrime 2` so a search for 'semiprime' finds nothing. `IsAtMostAlmostPrime` also lacks `mono` (`k ≤ l → … k n → … l n`).

  have hc : n.primeFactorsList.length = 2 := h.2
  obtain ⟨p, q, hf⟩ := List.length_eq_two.mp hc
  refine ⟨p, q, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList (n := n) (by simp [hf])
  · exact Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactorsList (n := n) (by simp [hf])
  · simpa [hf] using (Nat.prod_primeFactorsList h.1).symm

findings.claim: The module docstring says fundamental discriminants 'are exactly the discriminants of quadratic fields', but `IsFundamentalDiscr 1` holds. Including 1 is a standard convention, but no quadratic field has discriminant 1; Mathlib proves `2 < |discr K|` for degree > 1 (`NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two`). The gloss 'not a proper square multiple of a smaller discriminant' is also inaccurate for negative D: -12 = 2²·(-3) is excluded although -3 > -12 (it is |·| that is smaller), and it says nothing about 0, which the definition excludes.
findings.fix: Say 'the discriminants of quadratic fields, together with 1'; state primitivity as 'no D = f²e with f ≥ 2 and e ≡ 0, 1 mod 4'.

findings.claim: `Units.mem` inlines a general fact with no Mathlib name: in a number field of unit rank 0 every unit is torsion (L58-65 rebuild it from `exist_unique_eq_mul_prod` by emptying the product over `Fin (rank K)`). Stated as `NumberField.Units.mem_torsion_of_rank_eq_zero (h : rank K = 0) (u) : u ∈ torsion K` it has a 3-line proof and applies to every imaginary quadratic field.
findings.fix: Add `NumberField.Units.mem_torsion_of_rank_eq_zero` to Units/DirichletTheorem.lean and use it at L58-65.
findings.ev: hunts/cyclo-three/probe1.lean: `NumberField.Units.mem_torsion_of_rank_eq_zero` proved by `obtain ⟨⟨x, e⟩, hxu, -⟩ := exist_unique_eq_mul_prod _ u; have : IsEmpty (Fin (rank K)) := by rw [h]; infer_instance; simp [hxu]` compiles, exit 0; grep finds no rank-zero/torsion lemma under Mathlib/NumberTheory.

findings.claim: The three `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in` (on `lambda_sq` L81, `eta_sq` L90, `eq_one_or_neg_one_of_unit_of_congruent` L96) compensate for a missing simp lemma: Mathlib has `IsPrimitiveRoot.coe_toInteger : hζ.toInteger.1 = ζ` (Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:191) but no `algebraMap (𝓞 K) K hζ.toInteger = ζ`, which is the form `ext`/`simp` produce. Without the option and without that lemma, `simpa using hζ.isRoot_cyclotomic _` fails (`ζ ^ 2 + ζ + 1 = 0` vs `algebraMap (𝓞 K) K hζ.toInteger ^ 2 + … = 0`) and `ext; simp` at L124 leaves `↑⋯.toInteger = algebraMap (𝓞 K) K hζ.toInteger ^ 2`; with the lemma (`rfl`, tagged `@[simp]`) all three proofs compile with no `set_option`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] lemma IsPrimitiveRoot.algebraMap_toInteger (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ k) : algebraMap (𝓞 K) K hζ.toInteger = ζ := rfl` next to `coe_toInteger` and delete the three `set_option` lines (and the now unused `RingOfIntegers.neg_mk` at L117).
findings.ev: Module-mode copies of the file: hunts/cyclo-three/m0.lean (verbatim, exit 0); m1.lean (the three `set_option` lines deleted) fails at L86 and L92 with the type mismatch quoted and at L121 with an unsolved goal; m3.lean (m1 plus `@[simp] lemma IsPrimitiveRoot.algebraMap_toInteger' … := by rfl`) compiles, exit 0, with only `RingOfIntegers.neg_mk` reported unused. Non-module probe1.lean agrees: with `@[simp] IsPrimitiveRoot.algebraMap_toInteger' … := rfl`, `lambda_sq'`, `eta_sq'` and `eq_one_or_neg_one_of_unit_of_congruent'` compile without any `set_option` (exit 0). Without the lemma (first run of probe1 and probe2.lean) `lambda_sq'`/`eta_sq'` fail with the type mismatch quoted, and the third theorem fails at `ext; simp` with the unsolved goal quoted.

findings.claim: The module docstring states the Kummer-type result for units congruent to an integer 'modulo `3`', but only the `λ ^ 2` form exists, and the bridge `λ ^ 2 = -3 * η` is `private`, so callers cannot pass between the two. With `lambda_sq` public, `λ ^ 2 ∣ a ↔ 3 ∣ a` is a one-line `rw [lambda_sq hζ, Units.mul_right_dvd, neg_dvd]` (Astra A1 item 2).
findings.fix: Make `lambda_sq` public, add `lambda_sq_dvd_iff_three_dvd`, and state the modulo-3 corollary of `eq_one_or_neg_one_of_unit_of_congruent`.
findings.ev: hunts/cyclo-three/m3.lean (module mode): `example (a : 𝓞 K) : λ ^ 2 ∣ a ↔ (3 : 𝓞 K) ∣ a := by rw [lambda_sq hζ, _root_.Units.mul_right_dvd, neg_dvd]` compiles inside the file, exit 0.

findings.claim: `η ^ 2 + η + 1 = 0` (and with it `eta_sq`, `lambda_sq`) holds for a primitive cube root of unity in any domain, a one-liner from `IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_eq_zero`; Mathlib has no such general lemma (grep for `ζ ^ 2 + ζ + 1 = 0` finds nothing), so this file proves the 𝓞 K versions through `hζ.isRoot_cyclotomic` and coercions (Astra A1 item 3).
findings.fix: Add `IsPrimitiveRoot.sq_add_self_add_one (hz : IsPrimitiveRoot z 3) : z ^ 2 + z + 1 = 0` for `[CommRing R] [IsDomain R]` in RootsOfUnity and specialise.
findings.ev: hunts/cyclo-three/m3.lean: `example {R} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] {z : R} (hz : IsPrimitiveRoot z 3) : z ^ 2 + z + 1 = 0 := by simpa [Finset.sum_range_succ, add_comm, add_left_comm, add_assoc] using hz.geom_sum_eq_zero (by decide : 1 < 3)` compiles, exit 0.

findings.claim: The basic facts that justify the definition are missing: summability of ∑_p N(p)^{-s} and positivity of the denominator for s > 1, `HasDirichletDensity univ 1`, density 0 for finite sets, `HasDirichletDensity.unique`; and simp support (`primeIdealZetaSum ∅ s = 0`, `hasDirichletDensity_empty` is not simp).
findings.fix: Add the listed lemmas (the finite-set result needs `Tendsto (primeIdealZetaSum univ) (𝓝[>] 1) atTop`).

findings.claim: The docstring and the module's Main-results entry state the bound `∑_{p ∈ S} N(p)^{-s} ≤ #S` for every finite S without the theorem's hypothesis `0 ≤ s`, which is necessary (for a singleton {p} and s = -1 the sum is N(p) > 1); `primeIdealZetaSum` itself does not say it is 0 when the series is not summable (e.g. at s = 0 for infinite S), nor that 'partial' means restricted to S.
findings.fix: Add 'for s ≥ 0' in both places; document the tsum junk value of `primeIdealZetaSum`.

findings.claim: `HasDirichletDensity` is a `def` in a `public section` without `@[expose]` and has no characterisation lemma, so in any importing module it cannot be converted to or from its defining `Tendsto` statement (`exact h` is a type mismatch and `unfold HasDirichletDensity` fails): downstream code cannot prove that any set has a Dirichlet density, except `∅` via `hasDirichletDensity_empty`.
findings.fix: Add `hasDirichletDensity_iff : S.HasDirichletDensity δ ↔ Tendsto … (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 δ)` (or `@[expose]` the def).
findings.ev:
module
public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.NumberField.DirichletDensity
…
example (h : S.HasDirichletDensity δ) : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ S.primeIdealZetaSum s / primeIdealZetaSum (Set.univ : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 δ) := by exact h   -- error: Type mismatch
(and the converse; `unfold HasDirichletDensity at h` -- error: failed to unfold)

findings.claim: `invTransform_apply` exposes `invTransform F f` as a `tsum`, but the summability of that series (`invTransformSummable`) is private, so downstream users manipulating the sum must re-prove convergence; a public `hasSum_invTransform` is missing.
findings.fix: Make the summability public as `hasSum_invTransform : HasSum (fun i ↦ mahlerEquiv f i * F.coeff i) (invTransform F f)`.

findings.claim: The Kronecker-delta formula for the Mahler coefficients of a Mahler basis function, `PadicInt.mahlerEquiv ℤ_[p] (mahler n) i = if i = n then 1 else 0`, is buried as a local `have` here; it is basic Mahler-basis API and holds as a one-line `simp`.
findings.fix: Export it from NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean as a `@[simp]` lemma and use it here.
findings.ev:
example (n i : ℕ) : PadicInt.mahlerEquiv ℤ_[p] (mahler n) i = if i = n then 1 else 0 := by
  simp [PadicInt.mahlerEquiv_apply, ← fwdDiff_iter_choose_zero n i, fwdDiff_iter_eq_sum_shift, mahler_natCast_eq]

findings.claim: The module docstring describes an abstract measure as 'an R-linear functional on continuous maps X → R' with R 'a normed ring', but the definition is a *continuous* R-linear map C(X, R) →L[R] E into a module E, for any topological commutative ring R (no norm anywhere in the file); the `AbstractMeasure` docstring likewise speaks of the 'default (norm) topology', which is not a norm topology in this generality.
findings.fix: Module doc: 'a continuous R-linear map C(X, R) → E, for R a topological commutative ring and E a topological R-module'; drop '(norm)'.

findings.claim: The type synonym re-registers only `IsAddApply` and `IsSMulApply R`, not `IsZeroApply`, `IsNegApply`, `IsSubApply` or `IsSMulApply ℕ/ℤ` (all present on `C(X, R) →L[R] E`), so `simp` cannot evaluate `(0 : AbstractMeasure X R E) f = 0` or `(-μ) f = -μ f` ('simp made no progress').
findings.fix: Add the missing `Is*Apply` instances next to `isAddApply`.
findings.ev:

findings.fix: Replace the section variable by `[ContinuousConstSMul R E]`.
findings.ev:

findings.claim: The module docstring says 'if G is abelian and compact, then D(G, R) is a commutative ring', and the CommMonoid section says 'compact, Hausdorff, and commutative', but the `CommRing` instance also needs `[TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]` and `[T0Space R]` (i.e. G profinite): the Fubini lemma `prodMk_eq_prodMk'` it uses needs a totally disconnected factor. The docs claim commutativity for e.g. the circle group, which the file does not prove. The module overview also omits Hausdorffness. Without [T0Space R] the advertised claim can fail (Astra: G = ∏ℕ F₂, R = F₂ with the indiscrete topology, ultrafilter-evaluation functionals whose two iterated integrals of an indicator differ).
findings.fix: Say 'if G is a commutative profinite monoid (and R is T0)' in both places.

findings.claim: `WeakTopology` assumes `[NormedAddCommGroup E]` (and the section declares an unused `[ContinuousSMul R E]`), but the induced topology needs only `[AddCommGroup E] [TopologicalSpace E]`, the assumptions under which `AbstractMeasure X R E` itself makes sense.
findings.fix: Use `[AddCommGroup E] [TopologicalSpace E]` in the Weak section.

findings.claim: `StrongTopology` is documented as 'the topology induced by the norm', but the section's `[CompactSpace X]` is unused and so dropped from the exported definition: for non-compact X (e.g. X = ℕ discrete) C(X, R) is not normed and the topology is bounded convergence, which is not normable there.
findings.fix: Document it as the topology of bounded convergence, which is the operator-norm topology when X is compact.
findings.ev:
#check @AbstractMeasure.StrongTopology
-- {X R E} [TopologicalSpace X] [NontriviallyNormedField R] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace R E] → TopologicalSpace (AbstractMeasure X R E)   (no CompactSpace X)

findings.claim: `StrongTopology` assumes `[NontriviallyNormedField R] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace R E]`, but the bounded-convergence topology it inherits needs only `[NormedField R]` and a topological additive group E with `[Module R E]`.
findings.fix: Weaken the section variables.
findings.ev:
variable {X R E : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [NormedField R]
  [AddCommGroup E] [TopologicalSpace E] [IsTopologicalAddGroup E] [Module R E]
noncomputable def strongTopology' : TopologicalSpace (AbstractMeasure X R E) :=
  inferInstanceAs (TopologicalSpace (C(X, R) →L[R] E))

findings.claim: The module docstring describes `Nat.primeCounting'_add_le` as: 'all numbers greater than `k` and not coprime to `k` are not prime, and so only at most `φ(k)/k` fraction of the numbers from `k` to `n` are prime'. The theorem is about a second modulus `a < k`: `π' (k + n) ≤ π' k + φ a * (n / a + 1)`, i.e. numbers ≥ k not coprime to `a` are not prime, on the window `[k, k + n)`. The docstring's version (modulus `k` itself, window up to `n`) is a different bound from the one proved, and as a density claim it is false: `[30, 32)` has prime density 1/2 > φ(30)/30 = 8/30 (Astra A1 item 1).
findings.fix: Say: for `0 < a < k`, primes in `[k, k + n)` are coprime to `a`, so at most `φ a * (n / a + 1)` of them.
findings.ev: Measured: module docstring L29-31 vs statement L265-266 (`{a k : ℕ} (h0 : a ≠ 0) (h1 : a < k)`, bound `Nat.totient a * (n / a + 1)`).

findings.claim: Missing characteristic API: no successor formulas `π' (n + 1) = π' n + if n.Prime then 1 else 0` / `π (n + 1) = …`, no inclusive `π (nth Prime n) = n + 1` (only the strict `primeCounting'_nth_eq`), and `mem_primesBelow`, `mem_primesLE`, `primesBelow_card_eq_primeCounting'` are not `@[simp]` though the adjacent `primesLE_card_eq_primeCounting` is (Astra A1 items 3, 5). Astra also suggests `a.primeFactors ⊆ primesBelow k` instead of `a < k` in `primeCounting'_add_le` (not checked in Lean).
findings.fix: Add `primeCounting'_succ`, `primeCounting_succ`, `primeCounting_nth_eq`; tag the membership and card lemmas `@[simp]`.

findings.claim: Misstated by copy-paste: `BddLat.hom_id` (Order.Category.BddLat), `Lat.hom_id` (Order.Category.Lat) have exactly the same statement (Lean-checked), so `BddLat.hom_id` does not state what its name promises and the intended lemma is missing. The same bug affects BddLat.id_apply, hom_comp and comp_apply (l.95-104), which are all stated for Lat. Restate them for BddLat and BoundedLatticeHom instead of deprecating them. Astra rates it CRITICAL (a lemma weaker than or unrelated to its name).
findings.fix: Restate `BddLat.hom_id` as its name says (keep `Lat.hom_id`), or deprecate it if the intended lemma is not wanted.

findings.astraS: A2 (mis item 27, rating CRITICAL): The identity belongs to the wrong category and the RHS to the wrong bundled-hom type. Correct: `{X : BddLat} : (𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).hom = BoundedLatticeHom.id _`. The category instance immediately above explicitly constructs this bounded lattice homomorphism, so `rfl` supplies the intended statement. [Source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/e6bbacd0e1/Mathlib/Order/Category/BddLat.lean#L68-L100)
findings.res: Re-graded MAJOR→MINOR on 2026-10-07 by the user: a lemma whose name does not match its statement (here a copy-pasted neighbour) is a MINOR error; CRITICAL is reserved for wrong values/definitions like ModularForm.L.

findings.claim: The module docstring says a Bayes estimator 'can be written as a measurable function x ↦ argmin_y P†π(x)[θ ↦ ℓ θ y] for (P ∘ₘ π)-almost every x', but only the converse is proved (an argmin estimator is Bayes), and the stated direction is false in general: randomized estimators can be Bayes (constant loss, uniform choice of action), and with infinite Bayes risk every estimator is Bayes. The lower-integral reading of `∫⁻ x, ⨅ y, …` (the infimum need not be measurable) and the attainment hypothesis missing from the measurable-selection TODO are also undocumented.
findings.fix: State the proved direction: a measurable posterior minimiser defines a deterministic Bayes estimator; note the lower-integral convention and that selection needs the infimum to be attained.

findings.claim: `IsBayesEstimator ℓ P κ π := avgRisk ℓ P κ π = bayesRisk ℓ P π` does not require κ to be a Markov kernel, although an estimator is a Markov kernel and `bayesRisk` is the infimum over Markov kernels only. Non-estimators therefore qualify: the zero kernel whenever the Bayes risk is 0 (proved in Lean for 0-1 loss on Bool with a noiseless observation), and, with positive Bayes risk, a sub-probability kernel such as ½·δ_b on an action b of loss 2 when the best action has loss 1 (risk 1 = Bayes risk, while its normalisation δ_b has risk 2). No consumer depends on it yet; the only producer (`IsArgminEstimator.kernel`) is Markov.
findings.fix: Make it `IsMarkovKernel κ ∧ avgRisk … = bayesRisk …` (or a structure), or document that it is only meaningful for Markov κ.
findings.ev:
example : IsBayesEstimator (fun θ y : Bool ↦ if θ = y then (0 : ℝ≥0∞) else 1)
    (Kernel.id : Kernel Bool Bool) (0 : Kernel Bool Bool) (Measure.dirac true) := by
  have h0 : avgRisk (fun θ y : Bool ↦ if θ = y then (0 : ℝ≥0∞) else 1) Kernel.id 0 (Measure.dirac true) = 0 := by simp [avgRisk]
  have hB : bayesRisk (fun θ y : Bool ↦ if θ = y then (0 : ℝ≥0∞) else 1) Kernel.id (Measure.dirac true) = 0 := by
    refine le_antisymm ?_ bot_le
    refine (bayesRisk_le_avgRisk _ _ (Kernel.id : Kernel Bool Bool) _).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    simp [avgRisk, Kernel.id_apply]
  rw [IsBayesEstimator, h0, hB]

findings.claim: The module and definition docstrings (inherited by the `Ber(x, y, p)` notation) say the measure 'gives mass `p` to `{x}` and `1 - p` to `{y}`'. That is false when x = y (`Ber(0, 0, 0) {0} = 1`, not 0), and also for distinct points that the σ-algebra does not separate (indiscrete `Bool`: both singletons get mass 1). The definition is right; the docstring should state the mixture `p • δₓ + (1 - p) • δ_y`. The two `hasLaw_indicator_*` theorems also share one copied docstring.
findings.fix: Describe it as `p • dirac x + (1 - p) • dirac y`; qualify the singleton masses (x ≠ y, measurable singletons); give the second hasLaw theorem its own docstring.
findings.ev: example : Ber((0 : ℕ), 0, (0 : I)) {0} = 1 := by simp

findings.claim: Missing basic API: there is no symmetry lemma `Ber(x, y, p) = Ber(y, x, σ p)` (one `simp` line); the measurable-map version `map_bernoulliMeasure'` is not `@[simp]` (so `simp [hf]` makes no progress on `Ber(x, y, p).map f = Ber(f x, f y, p)`, unlike `map_dirac'`); and there are no evaluation lemmas for arbitrary (non-measurable) sets under `[MeasurableSingletonClass X]`.
findings.fix: Add `bernoulliMeasure_comm`/`_swap`, tag `map_bernoulliMeasure'` `@[simp]`, add `MeasurableSingletonClass` apply lemmas without `hs`.

example (x y : X) (p : I) : Ber(x, y, p) = Ber(y, x, σ p) := by
  simp [bernoulliMeasure_def, add_comm]   -- compiles

    Ber(x, y, p).map f = Ber(f x, f y, p) := by simp [hf]   -- error: simp made no progress

findings.claim: Several hypotheses are unnecessary: `map_bernoulliMeasure` needs no `[MeasurableSingletonClass Y]` (any f is a.e. equal to `f a` under `dirac a`); `bernoulliMeasure_apply_of_mem_of_mem` and its real version need no `hs : MeasurableSet s` (a Dirac measure gives 1 to any set containing its point); `eq_bernoulliMeasure` needs only `h1` and `h2` (`h3`, `h4` follow by complements in the probability measure μ). Astra also notes `[DecidablePred (· ∈ s)]` in the apply lemmas can be `[Decidable (x ∈ s)] [Decidable (y ∈ s)]` (not tested).
findings.fix: Drop the target singleton instance, `hs` in the both-atoms lemmas, and `h3 h4` (keep a four-case version only if wanted as `ext`).
findings.ev:
example [MeasurableSingletonClass X] (x y : X) (f : X → Y) (p : I) :
    Ber(x, y, p).map f = Ber(f x, f y, p) := by
  have hd (a : X) : (dirac a).map f = dirac (f a) := by
    calc (dirac a).map f = (dirac a).map (fun _ ↦ f a) := Measure.map_congr (ae_eq_dirac f)
      _ = dirac (f a) := by simp
  simp only [bernoulliMeasure_def]
  rw [AEMeasurable.map_add₀ (aemeasurable_dirac.smul_measure _)
    (aemeasurable_dirac.smul_measure _), Measure.map_smul, Measure.map_smul, hd, hd]
  all_goals exact aemeasurable_dirac
example (x y : X) (p : I) {s : Set X} (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) : Ber(x, y, p) s = 1 := by
  simp [bernoulliMeasure_def, hx, hy, ← ENNReal.coe_add]

findings.claim: `setBernoulli_singleton_of_not_subset` (`¬ s ⊆ u → setBer(u, p) {s} = 0`) sits in `section Countable`, but one excluded coordinate suffices: pick `i ∈ s \ u`; then `{s} ⊆ {t | i ∈ t}`, a measurable cylinder of measure `0`, with no countable union involved. The general version holds for every index type (e.g. `ι = ℝ`); the null-cylinder fact `setBer(u, p) {s | i ∈ s} = 0` for `i ∉ u` is itself missing as a lemma.

findings.claim: `(hs : MeasurableSet s)` can be weakened to `NullMeasurableSet s ((κ ⊗ₖ η) a)`. With `t := toMeasurable _ s`, `(κ ⊗ₖ η) a (t \ s) = 0`, so `ae_null_of_compProd_null` makes the slices of `s` and `t` have equal `η (a, b)`-measure for a.e. `b`. The function is then a.e. equal to a measurable one. The original statement is recovered via `hs.nullMeasurableSet`. This is low priority: the lemma has no consumers in Mathlib, and the Measure.prod analogue `integrable_measure_prodMk_left` has the same restriction.

findings.claim: The proof re-runs the whole L1-density Fubini argument (Integrable.induction plus the 8 compProd-only helpers Kernel.integral_fn_integral_add ... Kernel.continuous_integral_integral, L163-229, ~90 lines with this proof), but the statement follows in 12 lines from Kernel.integral_comp (same file, needs no s-finiteness and none of those helpers) via Kernel.compProd_apply_eq_compProd_sectR, Measure.compProd_eq_comp_prod, Measure.comp_eq_comp_const_apply, Kernel.prod_apply, Measure.dirac_prod and integral_map. A transitive-dependency walk confirms the derivation uses neither integral_compProd nor any compProd helper. The module docstring's reason for redoing the proofs ('the composition-product requires s-finiteness while the composition does not') only rules out deriving comp from compProd, not this direction. None of the 8 helpers has a consumer anywhere else in Mathlib (git grep origin/master).
findings.fix: Put the comp section first, prove integral_compProd from Kernel.integral_comp as in the probe, and deprecate the compProd-only scaffolding (or restate it as one-line corollaries).
findings.ev:
hunts/kernel-integral-compprod/batch1/Probe2.lean (compiles; #uses checks in Probe2.out):
theorem integral_compProd_via_comp {f : β × γ → E} (hf : Integrable f ((κ ⊗ₖ η) a)) :
    ∫ z, f z ∂(κ ⊗ₖ η) a = ∫ x, ∫ y, f (x, y) ∂η (a, x) ∂κ a := by
  have h_eq : (κ ⊗ₖ η) a =
      ((Kernel.id ×ₖ Kernel.sectR η a) ∘ₖ Kernel.const Unit (κ a)) () := by
    rw [Kernel.compProd_apply_eq_compProd_sectR, Measure.compProd_eq_comp_prod,
      Measure.comp_eq_comp_const_apply]
  rw [h_eq] at hf ⊢
  have h_ae := hf.ae_of_comp
  rw [Kernel.const_apply] at h_ae
  rw [Kernel.integral_comp hf, Kernel.const_apply]
  refine integral_congr_ae ?_
  filter_upwards [h_ae] with b hb
  rw [Kernel.prod_apply, Kernel.id_apply, Kernel.sectR_apply, Measure.dirac_prod] at hb ⊢
  exact integral_map measurable_prodMk_left.aemeasurable hb.aestronglyMeasurable

-- #uses integral_compProd_via_comp ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.continuous_integral_integral: false

-- #uses integral_compProd_via_comp ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.lintegral_fn_integral_sub: false
-- positive control: #uses ProbabilityTheory.integral_compProd ProbabilityTheory.Kernel.continuous_integral_integral: true

findings.claim: The hypothesis hs : MeasurableSet s is unnecessary. The statement holds for arbitrary s, given measurable t. The proof replaces s by toMeasurable (κ a) s: (κ a).restrict is unchanged, and ((κ ⊗ₖ η) a).restrict (s ×ˢ t) is unchanged because the defect set has a measurable section function supported on a measurable subset of toMeasurable s \ s. ht is genuinely needed (sketch, not formalised: κ a = Lebesgue on [0,1], η (a, x) = dirac x, t non-measurable with positive outer measure; then LHS = λ*(t) > 0 while RHS = ∫ 1_t = 0, since 1_t is not AEStronglyMeasurable). Its model MeasureTheory.setIntegral_prod needs neither. Consumers carrying the extra hypothesis: setIntegral_compProd_univ_right, MeasureTheory.Measure.setIntegral_compProd, 2 uses in Kernel/Disintegration/Integral.lean. The sibling Kernel.setLIntegral_compProd (CompProd.lean:389) likely admits the same weakening; that is unchecked.

findings.claim: The three `fn` lemmas `Kernel.integral_fn_integral_add_comp` (L354), `Kernel.integral_fn_integral_sub_comp` (L361) and `Kernel.lintegral_fn_integral_sub_comp` (L368) assume `Integrable f ((η ∘ₖ κ) a)` and `Integrable g ((η ∘ₖ κ) a)`, but their proofs only use the fibrewise consequences `hf.ae_of_comp : ∀ᵐ x ∂κ a, Integrable f (η x)` (and the same for `g`). With those weaker hypotheses the proofs go through unchanged, and the weakening is strict: for `κ = Kernel.const Unit Measure.count : Kernel Unit ℕ`, `η = Kernel.id`, `f = 1`, `f` is integrable on every fibre `η x = dirac x` but not on `(η ∘ₖ κ) () = count`. No kernel or completeness assumption is involved, so this is the only over-restriction. The same pattern is inherited from `MeasureTheory.integral_fn_integral_add`/`_sub`/`lintegral_fn_integral_sub` in `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Prod.lean` and the compProd copies at L163-L185.

findings.claim: The field `nonneg'` is implied by the other fields with no extra assumptions: `integrable` and `setIntegral` give `0 ≤ ∫ c in A, f (a, c) q ∂ν a = (κ a).real (…)` for every measurable A, so `ae_nonneg_of_forall_setIntegral_nonneg` yields `0 ≤ᵐ f (a, ·) q`. Dropping the field and deriving `IsRatCondKernelCDFAux.nonneg` this way leaves the whole file compiling. Under the finiteness assumptions that the only consumer (`isRatCondKernelCDF`: [IsFiniteKernel κ] [IsFiniteKernel ν]) and both constructors (CondCDF.isRatCondKernelCDFAux_preCDF, StandardBorel.isRatCondKernelCDFAux_density_Iic) work in, `mono'` (from `ae_le_of_forall_setIntegral_le` + `measureReal_mono`, needs κ finite) and `integrable` (from `measurable` + `nonneg'` + `le_one'` via `Integrable.of_bound`, needs ν finite) also follow. So every constructor must supply three derivable fields. (`le_one'` is not redundant: β = Bool, ν a = δ_true + δ_false, f(a,true) = 2F, f(a,false) = 0 satisfies all other fields.)

hunts/cdf-kernel/batch1/probe1.lean P7 and hunts/cdf-kernel/batch1/copy.lean:
lemma IsRatCondKernelCDFAux.integrable_iInf_rat_gt (hf : IsRatCondKernelCDFAux f κ ν)
    (a : α) (q : ℚ) :
    Integrable (fun t ↦ ⨅ r : Ioi q, f (a, t) r) (ν a) := by
  refine (hf.integrable a (q + 1)).mono'
    (Measurable.iInf fun _ ↦ hf.measurable_right a _).aestronglyMeasurable ?_
  filter_upwards [hf.bddBelow_range a, hf.nonneg a] with t hbdd h_nonneg
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (le_ciInf fun r ↦ h_nonneg _)]
  exact ciInf_le (hbdd q) ⟨q + 1, by simp⟩

No false theorem results: `setLIntegral`, `lintegral` and `compProd_toKernel` all assume `[IsFiniteKernel κ]`, and the probe shows that `setLIntegral` is false without it. theorem setLIntegral_toKernel_prod' [IsFiniteKernel κ] (hf : IsCondKernelCDF f κ ν)
    (a : α) {s : Set β} (hs : MeasurableSet s) {t : Set ℝ} (ht : MeasurableSet t) :

  have key {u : Set ℝ} (hu : MeasurableSet u) :

    rw [Measure.map_apply measurable_snd hu, Measure.restrict_apply (measurable_snd hu)]
    congr 1; ext; simp [and_comm]

  rw [← Measure.bind_apply ht hm, ← h, key ht]

findings.claim: `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` is not needed. For any measure, an a.e.-strongly-measurable `X` that is not in L² has `evariance X μ = ∞`. If `μ[X] = 0` this is immediate. If `μ[X] = c ≠ 0`, then `X` is integrable, and finite evariance would give `X - c ∈ L²`, so the constant `c` would be bounded by `2|X| + 4/|c|·(X-c)²` and hence integrable, which forces `μ` to be finite. Two downstream lemmas carry the hypothesis only because of this one and become hypothesis-free (beyond measurability): `variance_of_not_memLp` and `memLp_two_of_variance_ne_zero`. `evariance_eq_top_iff` and `evariance_lt_top_iff_memLp` still need it for their other direction.

findings.ev: hunts/variance/batch1/Probe1.lean, section P1: `theorem evariance_eq_top' (hXm : AEStronglyMeasurable X μ) (hX : ¬MemLp X 2 μ) : evariance X μ = ∞` proved with NO finiteness assumption (if X - μ[X] ∈ L² and μ[X] ≠ 0 then X is integrable, so univ ⊆ {|μ[X]|/2 ≤ ‖X‖} ∪ {|μ[X]|/2 ≤ ‖X - μ[X]‖} has finite measure by Integrable.measure_norm_ge_lt_top and MemLp.meas_ge_lt_top, hence memLp_const_iff gives the constant in L²); then `theorem variance_of_not_memLp' (hX : AEStronglyMeasurable X μ) (hX_not : ¬ MemLp X 2 μ) : variance X μ = 0 := by simp [variance, evariance_eq_top' hX hX_not]` and `theorem memLp_two_of_variance_ne_zero' (hX : AEStronglyMeasurable X μ) (h : Var[X; μ] ≠ 0) : MemLp X 2 μ := by contrapose h; exact variance_of_not_memLp' hX h` all compile (lake env lean, no errors in P1).

findings.claim: Astra argues (not formalised here) that several results are stated under `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` + `MemLp X 2 μ` where the primitive condition is `eVar[X; μ] ≠ ∞`: `ofReal_variance`, real Chebyshev `meas_ge_le_variance_div_sq` and `ae_eq_integral_of_variance_eq_zero` would apply to infinite measures under that condition (e.g. counting measure on ℕ with `X = 𝟙{0} - 𝟙{1}`); and the `IsZeroOrProbabilityMeasure` weakening also applies to `evariance_def'`, `variance_le_expectation_sq` and `variance_le_sq_of_bounded` (but not to `variance_le_sub_mul_sub`).
findings.fix: Add `eVar ≠ ∞` versions and derive the current forms; weaken the probability instance where the zero-measure case is trivial.

findings.claim: Docstrings drop the L² hypothesis that the statements carry: `ae_eq_integral_of_variance_eq_zero` says 'A random variable with variance `0` is almost surely constant' (the lemma needs `MemLp X 2 μ`), `IndepFun.variance_add` says the variance of an independent sum is the sum of the variances (needs `MemLp` for both), and the module's main-results list states `IndepFun.variance_add`/`variance_sum` and real Chebyshev without `MemLp X 2 μ` (and `0 < c`). Read literally with Mathlib's convention `Var[X] = 0` for infinite variance (`variance_of_not_memLp`), these summaries are false (a heavy-tailed `X` has `Var[X] = 0` without being a.s. constant).
findings.fix: Say 'An `L²` random variable …' in these docstrings and add the `MemLp`/`0 < c` hypotheses to the module's main-results summaries.
findings.ev: Doc-only finding: L161 docstring vs L162 `(hX : MemLp X 2 μ)`; L407 docstring vs L408 `(hX : MemLp X 2 μ)`; module docstring L27-34; `variance_of_not_memLp` gives `Var[X] = 0` for measurable non-L² `X`. Raised by Astra's A1 pass (items 2-3).

Consumers write `variance_nonneg _ _` by hand (StrongLaw.lean:433,459; Gaussian/Basic.lean:167,179,221; CentralLimitTheorem.lean:113; Fernique.lean:234).

As stated the lemma does not apply to a conditional measure `μ[|s]`, where `failed to synthesize IsProbabilityMeasure μ[|s]`, but the weakened version does. Being a probability measure (or zero) is necessary: for `μ = 2 • dirac`, `Var[fun _ ↦ 1] = 2 ≠ 0 = Var[0]`.

findings.claim: `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` can be weakened to `[IsZeroOrProbabilityMeasure μ]`, since the statement is trivial for `μ = 0`. Kernel fibres of an `IsZeroOrMarkovKernel` have this weaker instance, and Moments/Basic.lean already uses it (`centralMoment_one`, `cgf_zero`). It cannot be weakened to `IsFiniteMeasure`: for `μ = 2 • dirac ()`, `Var[fun _ ↦ 0 - 1; μ] ≠ Var[fun _ ↦ 0; μ]`, which was checked in Lean. The `AEStronglyMeasurable` hypothesis is needed: a non-measurable indicator gives different junk lintegrals for `X` and `X - c`. This was argued on paper, not in Lean.

findings.claim: `variance_dirac` assumes `[MeasurableSingletonClass Ω]`, but `Var[X; Measure.dirac x] = 0` also holds for every measurable `X` on any measurable space. Mathlib has such companions for integrals (`integral_dirac'` with `StronglyMeasurable f`, `lintegral_dirac'` with `Measurable f`), but the variance has none. (The class cannot simply be dropped: without it and without measurability of `X`, `μ[X]` and `∫⁻` take junk/lower-integral values. This was argued on paper, not checked in Lean.)
findings.fix: Add `variance_dirac' (x : Ω) (hX : Measurable X) : Var[X; Measure.dirac x] = 0`, proved by `rw [variance_congr (ae_eq_dirac' hX)]; simp [variance, evariance]`.
findings.ev:
hunts/variance/batch4/probe1.lean theorems P4a/P4b, e.g.
theorem P4a (x : Ω) (hX : Measurable X) : Var[X; Measure.dirac x] = 0 := by
  rw [variance_congr (ae_eq_dirac' hX)]
  simp [variance, evariance]
(also added as `variance_dirac'` in hunts/variance/batch4/VarianceEdit.lean, which compiles)

findings.claim: The proof uses only the a.e. content of `MeasurePreserving X μ ν` (`hX.aemeasurable`, `hX.map_eq`), so it does not need `Measurable X`. The a.e. companion is missing: HasLaw.lean has `HasLaw.covariance_comp` and `HasLaw.covariance_fun_comp`, but for the variance it has only `HasLaw.variance_eq`, which covers just the case `f = id`. There is no `HasLaw.variance_comp` or `HasLaw.variance_fun_comp` (checked with git grep).
findings.fix: Add `HasLaw.variance_fun_comp (hY : HasLaw Y ν μ) (hf : AEMeasurable f ν) : Var[fun ω ↦ f (Y ω); μ] = Var[f; ν]` and its `∘` form to HasLaw.lean, matching the covariance pair.
findings.ev:
hunts/variance/batch4/probe1.lean theorem P5:
theorem P5 {𝓧 : Type*} {m𝓧 : MeasurableSpace 𝓧} {ν : Measure 𝓧} {Y : Ω → 𝓧}
    (hY : HasLaw Y ν μ) {f : 𝓧 → ℝ} (hf : AEMeasurable f ν) :
    Var[fun ω ↦ f (Y ω); μ] = Var[f; ν] := by
  rw [← hY.map_eq, variance_map (hY.map_eq ▸ hf) hY.aemeasurable, Function.comp_def]

findings.claim: The lemma needs `Y : Ω' ≃ᵐ Ω`, but the same one-line proof works for any `MeasurableEmbedding Y` (through `MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map` and `MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map`). That is the generality Mathlib uses for `integral_map` and `lintegral_map` on embeddings. `covariance_map_equiv` has the same restriction.
findings.fix: Add `MeasurableEmbedding.variance_map (hY : MeasurableEmbedding Y) (X : Ω → ℝ) : Var[X; μ.map Y] = Var[X ∘ Y; μ]` and derive `variance_map_equiv` as `Y.measurableEmbedding.variance_map X`. Do the same for covariance.

hunts/variance/batch4/probe1.lean theorem P2:
theorem P2 {Ω' : Type*} {mΩ' : MeasurableSpace Ω'} {μ : Measure Ω'} (X : Ω → ℝ) {Y : Ω' → Ω}

findings.claim: The proof (L343–L360, 18 lines) works out the non-L² case by hand, through `evariance_eq_lintegral_ofReal`, `integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae`, two nested `by_cases`, and a rebuilt `MemLp` argument. The in-file lemma `variance_of_not_memLp` already gives `Var[X; μ] = 0` in that case, and with it the proof is 5 lines.
findings.fix: Replace the proof with `by_cases hX : MemLp X 2 μ; · rw [variance_eq_sub hX]; exact sub_le_self _ (sq_nonneg _); · rw [variance_of_not_memLp hm hX]; exact integral_nonneg fun _ ↦ sq_nonneg _`.
findings.ev:
hunts/variance/batch4/probe1.lean theorem P3:
theorem P3 [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hm : AEStronglyMeasurable X μ) :
    variance X μ ≤ μ[X ^ 2] := by
  by_cases hX : MemLp X 2 μ
  · rw [variance_eq_sub hX]
    exact sub_le_self _ (sq_nonneg _)
  · rw [variance_of_not_memLp hm hX]
    exact integral_nonneg fun _ ↦ sq_nonneg _
(also substituted in hunts/variance/batch4/VarianceEdit.lean, which compiles)

findings.claim: The hypothesis `hX : AEStronglyMeasurable X μ` is not needed. If `X` is not a.e.-strongly measurable, then `μ[X] = 0` by `integral_undef`, and both sides reduce to `∫⁻ ω, ‖X ω‖ₑ ^ 2 ∂μ`. So the identity holds for every `X` under `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]`.
findings.fix: Drop `hX` and handle the non-measurable case first with `simp [evariance, integral_undef (fun h ↦ hX h.1)]`. The lemma has no consumers in Mathlib.
findings.ev:
hunts/variance/batch4/probe1.lean theorem P1:
theorem P1 [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : Ω → ℝ) :
    evariance X μ = (∫⁻ ω, ‖X ω‖ₑ ^ 2 ∂μ) - ENNReal.ofReal (μ[X] ^ 2) := by
  by_cases hX : AEStronglyMeasurable X μ
  · exact evariance_def' hX
  · simp [evariance, integral_undef (fun h ↦ hX h.1)]
(also applied to the declaration in hunts/variance/batch4/VarianceEdit.lean, which compiles)

section TVS
variable {E F : Type*} [TopologicalSpace E] [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] {mE : MeasurableSpace E}
  [TopologicalSpace F] [AddCommGroup F] [Module ℝ F] {mF : MeasurableSpace F}
  {μ : Measure E} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ν : Measure F} [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
lemma variance_dual_prod'_tvs {L : StrongDual ℝ (E × F)}
    (hLμ : MemLp (L.comp (.inl ℝ E F)) 2 μ) (hLν : MemLp (L.comp (.inr ℝ E F)) 2 ν) :
    Var[L; μ.prod ν] = Var[L.comp (.inl ℝ E F); μ] + Var[L.comp (.inr ℝ E F); ν] := by
  have : L = fun x : E × F ↦ L.comp (.inl ℝ E F) x.1 + L.comp (.inr ℝ E F) x.2 := by
    ext; rw [L.comp_inl_add_comp_inr]
  rw [this, variance_add_prod hLμ hLν]
end TVS

findings.claim: The `limitProcess` docstring says it picks g when "g is ⨆ t, 𝓕 t-measurable (i.e. HasLimitProcess X 𝓕 P holds)", but `HasLimitProcess` requires strong measurability, strictly stronger for non-separable codomains; the module docstring claims a strongly adapted process has a strongly measurable limit, which needs a countably generated atTop and a metrizable codomain; both cite `Submartingale.ae_tendsto_limitProcess` without its real-valued, ℕ-indexed scope; and the degenerate case atTop = ⊥ (e.g. ι empty), where every process has a limit process, is undocumented.
findings.fix: 'strongly measurable'; qualify the module motivation; state the scope of the cited theorem.

findings.claim: Redundant or too-narrow hypotheses: `memLp_limitProcess_of_eLpNorm_bdd`'s `hfm` (a.e.-strong measurability) follows from the finite bound `hbdd` via `aestronglyMeasurable_of_eLpNorm_ne_top`; `limitProcess_prodMk` forces both processes to take values in the same E although the same one-line proof covers `X : ι → Ω → E`, `Z : ι → Ω → F` (as `HasLimitProcess.prodMk` already does).
findings.fix: Drop `hfm`; generalise `limitProcess_prodMk` to two codomains.
findings.ev:
example … (hbdd : ∀ n, eLpNorm (X n) p P ≤ R) : MemLp (limitProcess X 𝓕 P) p P :=
  memLp_limitProcess_of_eLpNorm_bdd
    (fun n ↦ aestronglyMeasurable_of_eLpNorm_ne_top ((hbdd n).trans_lt ENNReal.coe_lt_top).ne) hbdd
example … {X : ι → Ω → E} {Z : ι → Ω → F} (hX : HasLimitProcess X 𝓕 P) (hZ : HasLimitProcess Z 𝓕 P) :
    𝓕.limitProcess (fun t ω ↦ (X t ω, Z t ω)) P =ᵐ[P] fun ω ↦ (𝓕.limitProcess X P ω, 𝓕.limitProcess Z P ω) :=
  hX.limitProcess_comp₂ (f := fun x y ↦ (x, y)) continuous_id hZ

The projective-resolution packaging belongs only in `coindIso`.

findings.claim: `coindIso : Hⁿ(G, Coind_S^G A) ≅ Hⁿ(S, A)` is built abstractly through resolutions, and the file proves nothing about it: no lemma identifies its forward map with the classical Shapiro map (restriction to S followed by evaluation at 1, i.e. `groupCohomology.map S.subtype (resCoindAdjunction.counit.app A) n`), no naturality in A (no `NatIso` `coindFunctor ⋙ functor k G n ≅ functor k S n`), no compatibility with `δ`, and no component simp lemmas for the helper. Mathlib has no other declaration mentioning it, so a user cannot compute with it on cocycles.
findings.fix: Prove `coindIso_hom_eq_map` (restriction + counit), package coefficient naturality as a NatIso, add `@[simps]` to the helper.
findings.ev: -- git grep 'coindIso\b' finds only Rep.coindIso (Coinduced.lean, a different iso) besides this file's definition; no lemma has groupCohomology.coindIso in its statement

findings.claim: The module docstring's "Main definitions" entry swaps the roles of `R` and `S`: it says "if `R` is `I`-adically complete, then a compatible family of ring maps `S →+* R ⧸ I ^ n` can be lifted to … `S →+* R`", while `IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom` needs `S` complete and lifts `f n : R →+* S ⧸ I ^ n` to `R →+* S` (as the file's own opening paragraph says). It also cites `mk_liftRingHom_apply`, which does not exist (the lemma is `mk_liftRingHom`).
findings.fix: Swap `R`/`S` in the bullet and cite `mk_liftRingHom`.
findings.ev: Source L13–25 vs. L32–50; `git grep mk_liftRingHom_apply origin/master -- Mathlib`: only the docstring.

findings.claim: `IsAdicComplete.algHom_ext` (two algebra maps into `S` agreeing modulo every `I ^ n` are equal) assumes `[IsAdicComplete I S]` and commutative rings `R`, `A`, but only Hausdorffness is used: under `[IsHausdorff I S]`, `[CommSemiring K] [Semiring A]` it is `DFunLike.coe_injective` + `IsHausdorff.funext'`. Its current proof detours through `ofAlgEquiv`; e.g. `S = ℤ`, `I = (2)` (separated, not complete) is excluded.
findings.fix: Restate as `IsHausdorff.algHom_ext` under `[IsHausdorff I S]` with the 4-line proof, keeping the complete version as an alias.
findings.ev: probe2.lean: the `[IsHausdorff I S]`/`CommSemiring`/`Semiring` version compiles; applying `IsAdicComplete.algHom_ext` with only `[IsHausdorff I S]` fails to synthesize `IsAdicComplete I S`.

findings.claim: Duplicate declarations: `BialgEquiv.coe_toCoalgEquiv` (RingTheory.Bialgebra.Equiv), `BialgEquiv.coe_toAlgEquiv` (RingTheory.Bialgebra.Equiv) state exactly the same thing (Lean-checked). findings.claim: `groupLikeSubmonoid R A` has no membership lemma: `a ∈ groupLikeSubmonoid R A ↔ IsGroupLikeElem R a` holds by `Iff.rfl`, but `simp` makes no progress on it. Nothing in Mathlib uses the submonoid, so the missing `mem_groupLikeSubmonoid` is the only way in.

findings.ev: probe1.lean L8 `example : a ∈ groupLikeSubmonoid R A ↔ IsGroupLikeElem R a := by simp` → `simp` made no progress; L9 `Iff.rfl` compiles.

findings.claim: The file builds the same monoid twice: `groupLikeSubmonoid R A` (whose coercion type `↥(groupLikeSubmonoid R A)` is already a monoid) and the structure `GroupLike R A`, with `One`, `Mul`, `Pow`, `Monoid` and `CommMonoid` instances transported by hand along `val_injective`. No `MulEquiv` connects the two (the coalgebra file's `GroupLike.valEquiv` to the subtype is a plain `Equiv`), and neither has any consumer of the other, so facts proved for one cannot be used on the other.
findings.fix: Either add `GroupLike.mulEquivSubmonoid : GroupLike R A ≃* groupLikeSubmonoid R A` (upgrading `valEquiv`), or derive the `GroupLike` monoid structure from the submonoid through that equivalence.
findings.ev: `grep -rnw 'groupLikeSubmonoid\|valMonoidHom'` outside the file: no hits; `grep 'GroupLike R A ≃\*'`: no hits. The only bridge is `GroupLike.valEquiv : GroupLike R A ≃ Subtype (IsGroupLikeElem R)` in `Coalgebra/GroupLike.lean:88`.

findings.claim: The module introduction and the `IsDedekindDomainInv` docstring say 'all fractional ideals are invertible' / 'every fractional ideal has an inverse', omitting 'nonzero' (0 is a fractional ideal and 0 * 0⁻¹ = 0). Proof comments are stale: 'minimal set'/'contained in J' (it is a multiset and I), and `mul_inv_cancel_of_le_one` cites `exists_notMem_one_of_ne_bot`, a downstream lemma in Ideal/Lemmas.lean, though it uses `not_inv_le_one_of_ne_bot`; 'Main definitions' lists a theorem.
findings.fix: Add 'nonzero'; state the exact property about M; refresh the comments.

findings.claim: Several results assume Dedekind where much less is used: `Ideal.finiteMultiplicity` holds in every Noetherian domain (Krull intersection `Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isDomain`); `PrimeSpectrum.exists_multiset_prod_cons_le_and_prod_not_le` needs only `[IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Ring.DimensionLEOne A]` (a copy with that binder compiles), so it also covers non-normal domains like k[t²,t³]. Astra also notes (untested) that its `hNF : ¬IsField A` follows from `hI0`, `hIM` and maximality, and that `adjoinIntegral_eq_one_of_isUnit` holds over any localization.
findings.fix: State `finiteMultiplicity` for Noetherian domains (near Filtration) and weaken the prime-product lemma's binder.
findings.ev:
example {B : Type*} [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    {I J : Ideal B} (hI : I ≠ ⊤) (hJ : J ≠ ⊥) : FiniteMultiplicity I J := by
  by_contra h
  have hd : ∀ n : ℕ, I ^ n ∣ J := FiniteMultiplicity.not_iff_forall.mp h
  apply hJ
  apply eq_bot_iff.mpr
  rw [← Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isDomain I hI]
  exact le_iInf fun n => Ideal.le_of_dvd (hd n)

findings.claim: Intended alias proved twice: `RingHom.FiniteType.of_finite` (RingTheory.FiniteType), `RingHom.Finite.finiteType` (RingTheory.FiniteType) state exactly the same thing (Lean-checked); the second name is wanted (e.g. for dot notation) but is re-proved instead of declared with `alias`. There is already `alias RingHom.Finite.to_finiteType := of_finite` at line 253, so this is a third name. Make Finite.finiteType an alias and drop or deprecate one of the two dot-notation names.

findings.claim: `RingHom.finrank_comp_left_of_bijective` assumes `h1 : f.Finite` and `h2 : f.Flat`, but `(g.comp f).finrank = f.finrank` holds for every `f` when `g` is bijective: T ≃ S as R-algebras, and `Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv` needs no hypotheses. These assumptions propagate to `Scheme.Hom.finrank_comp_left_of_isIso` in FlatRank.lean.
findings.fix: Drop `h1 h2`; prove by `algebraize` and `Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv (AlgEquiv.ofBijective (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S T) hg).toLinearEquiv`.
findings.ev:
example {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]
    (f : R →+* S) (g : S →+* T) (hg : Function.Bijective g) (x : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    (g.comp f).finrank x = f.finrank x := by
  algebraize [f, g, (g.comp f)]
  exact congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv
    (AlgEquiv.ofBijective (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R S T) hg).toLinearEquiv).symm x

findings.claim: `Submodule.exists_eq_colon_of_mem_minimalPrimes` has a 66-line proof (L34-99) in one block: the existence of `n` and `J` with `I ^ n * J ≤ ann`, `¬ J ≤ I` (L40-52), the finite-product construction of `z` (L73-91) and the final minimality argument are independent steps that would read better as separate lemmas (the first is a general statement about minimal primes of an ideal in a Noetherian ring).
findings.fix: Extract the `key` step as a lemma about minimal primes in a Noetherian ring (`∃ n ≠ 0, ∃ J, I ^ n * J ≤ a ∧ ¬ J ≤ I` for `I ∈ a.minimalPrimes`) and the product step as a helper.
findings.ev: Measured: the proof spans L34-L99 (66 lines) of the audited file; profiling with `-Dprofiler=true -Dprofiler.threshold=100` reports no declaration over 100 ms, so this is a structure finding, not a speed one.

findings.claim: Astra argues (not formalised here) that `[IsNoetherianRing R]` is stronger than needed: finite generation of the chosen prime `I` suffices (a finitely generated weakly associated prime is associated, Stacks 058A), e.g. `R = k[t, z₁, z₂, …]`, `N = (t²)`, `x = 1`, `I = (t)` is covered by an `I.FG` version but not by the current theorem. Some finiteness is necessary (`k[X₁, X₂, …]/(X₁², X₂², …)` is a counterexample without any).
findings.fix: Prove a version assuming `I.FG` and derive the Noetherian one.
findings.ev: Suspected: Astra's A1 item 1 (paper argument via ideal saturation); not formalised here.

findings.claim: The proof establishes the stronger `∃ a : R, I = N.colon {a • x}` (the witness is `y • x` for a scalar `y`, L68) but the theorem exports only `∃ x' : M, I = N.colon {x'}`, so callers lose the guarantee that the witness lies in `R ∙ x` (e.g. for `M = 𝔽₂²`, `N = ⊥`, `x = (1, 0)` the weak conclusion also allows `(0, 1)`).
findings.fix: State the theorem as `∃ a : R, I = N.colon {a • x}` (changing the witness at L68 to `y`) and keep the current form as a one-line corollary.
findings.ev: hunts/minprime-colon/probe_strong.lean: the file with the conclusion `∃ a : R, I = N.colon {a • x}`, the witness `⟨y, …⟩` and the corollary `exists_eq_colon_of_mem_minimalPrimes'` (the current statement) compiles with exit 0. Raised by Astra's A1 pass (item 2).

findings.claim: The module overview states the universal property as `Hom_R(Ω[S⁄R], M) ≃ₗ[S] Der_R(S, M)`; it must be `Hom_S`. `linearMapEquivDerivation` itself is correctly about `Ω[S⁄R] →ₗ[S] M`, and an R-linear map out of Ω need not give a derivation: for R = ℚ, S = M = ℚ[X], the ℚ-linear F(p dX) = p' composes with d to second differentiation, which fails Leibniz.
findings.fix: Write `Hom_S(Ω[S⁄R], M) ≃ₗ[S] Der_R(S, M)`.

findings.claim: The name says `one_smul_sub_smul_one`, but the statement is about tensors: `(1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] a - a ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : S) ∈ ideal R S`. Read literally, the name describes `1 • a - a • 1`, which is always 0. Mathlib's sibling lemma for the same expression uses `tmul`: `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.one_tmul_sub_tmul_one_mul_elem : (1 ⊗ₜ s - s ⊗ₜ 1) * elem R S = 0` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Unramified/Finite.lean:143). The name is used 9 times in Basic.lean and nowhere else.
findings.fix: Rename to `KaehlerDifferential.one_tmul_sub_tmul_one_mem_ideal` and keep the old name as a `@[deprecated]` alias.

All three compile unchanged (same bodies and proofs) under `[CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring S] [AddCommMonoid M]`. The general version specialises back to the file's by `rfl`.

Every caller passes it by hand: Extension/Cotangent/Basic.lean:188 and :300, and Kaehler/TensorProduct.lean:171 and :194. Mathlib's equivalent `LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul` is `@[simp]`. findings.claim: The 20-line proof is brittle. It uses `refine TensorProduct.inductionOn ... ; swap` twice, two 9-lemma `rw` chains (`add_mul, map_add, map_add, map_add, add_smul, smul_add, h₁, h₂, add_add_add_comm`), a non-terminal bare `dsimp`, and a closing `simp only` with hand-instantiated `mul_comm (x * y) x₁` and `mul_right_comm x₁ x₂`. A structural `induction ... with` proof that ends with `module` is 9 lines and compiles.
findings.fix: Replace the proof with the `induction x with | add => simp only [...]; abel | tmul => induction y with ... | tmul => simp only [tmul_mul_tmul, tensorProductTo_tmul, lmul'_apply_tmul, Derivation.leibniz]; module` version.
findings.ev:
batch0/probe6_golf.lean (G1):
  induction x with
  | add _ _ h₁ h₂ => simp only [add_mul, map_add, h₁, h₂, add_smul, smul_add]; abel
  | tmul x₁ x₂ =>
    induction y with
    | add _ _ h₁ h₂ => simp only [mul_add, map_add, h₁, h₂, add_smul, smul_add]; abel
    | tmul y₁ y₂ =>
      simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, Derivation.tensorProductTo_tmul,
        TensorProduct.lmul'_apply_tmul, Derivation.leibniz]
      module

findings.claim: `fromIdeal` (the quotient map `I →ₗ Ω[S⁄R]`) has no API except `fromIdeal_surjective`: no equality or kernel lemma. The cotangent API does not fire on it: `rw [Ideal.toCotangent_eq]` and `simp [Ideal.toCotangent_eq_zero]` fail on `fromIdeal` goals. As a result the file bypasses `fromIdeal` and states `DLinearMap_apply`, `D_apply`, `liftKaehlerDifferential_apply` and `D_tensorProductTo` through `(ideal R S).toCotangent`, whose codomain is `(ideal R S).Cotangent`, not `Ω[S⁄R]`. It is used only 3 times, all in this file. The missing lemma `fromIdeal_eq_iff` is one line.
findings.fix: Add `fromIdeal_eq_iff : fromIdeal R S x = fromIdeal R S y ↔ (x - y : S ⊗[R] S) ∈ ideal R S ^ 2 := Ideal.toCotangent_eq _` (and an `_eq_zero_iff`), and state the file's apply lemmas through `fromIdeal`.
findings.ev: batch0/probe7_fromIdeal.lean: `example (x y : ideal R S) : fromIdeal R S x = fromIdeal R S y ↔ (x - y : S ⊗[R] S) ∈ ideal R S ^ 2 := by rw [Ideal.toCotangent_eq]` fails with `rewrite failed: did not find (Ideal.toCotangent ?I) ?x = ...`, and `example (x : ideal R S) : fromIdeal R S x = 0 ↔ (x : S ⊗[R] S) ∈ ideal R S ^ 2 := by simp [Ideal.toCotangent_eq_zero]` gives `simp made no progress`. The one-liners `theorem fromIdeal_eq_iff ... := Ideal.toCotangent_eq _` and `theorem fromIdeal_eq_zero_iff ... := Ideal.toCotangent_eq_zero _ x` compile.

findings.claim: The statement equates `DLinearMap R S s : Ω[S⁄R]` with `(ideal R S).toCotangent ⟨…⟩ : (ideal R S).Cotangent`, which type-checks only by unfolding the semireducible `def KaehlerDifferential`. After `rw [DLinearMap_apply]` the goal is not type-correct at `implicit` transparency, and the next generic step fails: `rw [← map_add]` and `rw [← LinearMap.map_smul_of_tower (ideal R S).toCotangent]` both fail. This is the failure the adaptation note before `D` (lines 190–221) works around with three `backward.*` options and a `have : CompatibleSMul …`. Stated through `fromIdeal` (defeq, so still `rfl`), the same rewrites succeed. In a copy of the file, restating it this way, adding `fromIdeal_eq_iff`, and rewriting `D`'s proof through `fromIdeal` lets all three `set_option backward.*` lines and the `have` go, and the whole file compiles. (`D_apply`, line 246, in batch 1, has the same shape.)
findings.fix: State `DLinearMap_apply` (and `D_apply`) as `… = fromIdeal R S ⟨1 ⊗ₜ s - s ⊗ₜ 1, _⟩`, add `fromIdeal_eq_iff`, and rewrite `D`'s proof through `fromIdeal`. This removes the backward options and the adaptation note.
findings.ev: batch0/probe4_synonym_use.lean: U1 `example (s t : S) : DLinearMap R S s + DLinearMap R S t = DLinearMap R S (s + t) := by rw [DLinearMap_apply, DLinearMap_apply, DLinearMap_apply, ← map_add]` fails (`did not find ?f ?x + ?f ?y`; note: target not type-correct under `implicit` transparency: `(ideal R S).toCotangent ⟨…⟩ has type (ideal R S).Cotangent but is expected to have type Ω[S⁄R]`). U3 `rw [DLinearMap_apply, ← LinearMap.map_smul_of_tower (ideal R S).toCotangent]` fails the same way. U2 and U4 run the same rewrites through `DLinearMap_apply_fromIdeal (s) : DLinearMap R S s = fromIdeal R S ⟨1 ⊗ₜ s - s ⊗ₜ 1, _⟩ := rfl` and compile. Whole-file check: batch0/KB_fromIdeal.lean (diff in batch0/KB_fromIdeal.diff) drops the 3 `set_option backward.*` lines and the `CompatibleSMul` `have` from `D`, compiles, and `#print axioms KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange_surjective` runs at the end.

findings.claim: The 13-line tactic-mode construction (`liftQ` ∘ `restrictScalarsEquiv.symm` plus a `smul_induction_on` kernel proof) re-implements Mathlib's `Ideal.Cotangent.lift (f : I →ₗ[R] M) (hf : ∀ (x y : I), f (x * y) = 0) : I.Cotangent →ₗ[R] M` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Cotangent.lean:234). A 3-line term-mode definition via `Ideal.Cotangent.lift` is equal to it (by `ext a; rfl`, though not `rfl` as bundled maps), keeps `liftKaehlerDifferential_apply` true by `rfl`, and the whole file compiles with it substituted.
findings.fix: Define `liftKaehlerDifferential D` as `Ideal.Cotangent.lift (D.tensorProductTo.comp ((ideal R S).subtype.restrictScalars S)) fun x y => by simp [Derivation.tensorProductTo_mul, RingHom.mem_ker.mp x.2, RingHom.mem_ker.mp y.2]`.
findings.ev:
-- hunts/kaehler/batch1/probeE.lean
noncomputable def liftViaCotangentLift (D : Derivation R S M) : Ω[S⁄R] →ₗ[S] M :=
  Ideal.Cotangent.lift (D.tensorProductTo.comp ((ideal R S).subtype.restrictScalars S))
    fun x y => by
      simp [Derivation.tensorProductTo_mul, RingHom.mem_ker.mp x.2, RingHom.mem_ker.mp y.2]
example (D : Derivation R S M) : liftViaCotangentLift D = D.liftKaehlerDifferential := by
  ext a; rfl
example (D : Derivation R S M) (x : ideal R S) :
    liftViaCotangentLift D ((ideal R S).toCotangent x) = D.tensorProductTo x := rfl
-- and hunts/kaehler/batch1/v8_cotangentLift.lean (full file with this definition substituted): EXIT=0

findings.claim: The hypothesis `Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B)` is used only to get `Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A]` (via `subsingleton_of_surjective`). The same proof works under `[Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A]]`, which is in fact equivalent to the conclusion (`Surjective (mapBaseChange R A B) ↔ Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A]` compiles). The general form covers formally unramified extensions: étale algebras and localisations, where `algebraMap` is not surjective. There the current lemma cannot be applied, so `KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale` (Etale/Kaehler.lean:39) re-derives surjectivity inline from `exact_mapBaseChange_map` and `Subsingleton.elim`.
findings.fix: Add `mapBaseChange_surjective_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A]]` (and the iff), derive `mapBaseChange_surjective` from it, and use it in `tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale`.
findings.ev:
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Kaehler.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Unramified.Basic

open KaehlerDifferential TensorProduct

variable (R A B : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B]
  [Algebra R B] [IsScalarTower R A B]

/-- Same proof as `mapBaseChange_surjective`, with `Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A]` in place of
surjectivity of `algebraMap A B`. -/
theorem mapBaseChange_surjective_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A]] :
    Function.Surjective (mapBaseChange R A B) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, range_mapBaseChange, ← top_le_iff]
  exact fun x _ ↦ Subsingleton.elim _ _

-- the current lemma is a special case
example (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B)) :
    Function.Surjective (mapBaseChange R A B) :=
  have := subsingleton_of_surjective A B h
  mapBaseChange_surjective_of_subsingleton R A B

-- and the hypothesis is in fact necessary: surjectivity of `mapBaseChange` is equivalent to it
theorem mapBaseChange_surjective_iff :
    Function.Surjective (mapBaseChange R A B) ↔ Subsingleton Ω[B⁄A] := by
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨fun x y ↦ ?_⟩, fun _ ↦ mapBaseChange_surjective_of_subsingleton R A B⟩
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := map_surjective R A B x
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := map_surjective R A B y
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := h x
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := h y
  rw [(exact_mapBaseChange_map R A B _).mpr ⟨x, rfl⟩,
    (exact_mapBaseChange_map R A B _).mpr ⟨y, rfl⟩]

-- covers formally unramified (e.g. étale, localisation) extensions, where `algebraMap A B`
-- need not be surjective; `Etale/Kaehler.lean` reproves this inline today
example [Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B] : Function.Surjective (mapBaseChange R A B) :=
  mapBaseChange_surjective_of_subsingleton R A B

-- `mapBaseChange_surjective` itself cannot be applied there:
example [Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B] : Function.Surjective (mapBaseChange R A B) :=
  mapBaseChange_surjective R A B

-- result: everything compiles except the last `example`, which fails as expected (type mismatch: needs `Function.Surjective ⇑(algebraMap A B)`)

variable {σ τ : Type*} {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]

    (f.toMvPowerSeries i).subst a = f.subst (a i) := by
  rw [toMvPowerSeries_eq_subst, PowerSeries.subst, MvPowerSeries.subst_comp_subst_apply
    (PowerSeries.HasSubst.const (PowerSeries.HasSubst.X _)) ha, MvPowerSeries.subst_X ha,

findings.fix: Move it next to `toMvPowerSeries_inj` under `[CommSemiring R]` and prove it from `MvPowerSeries.coeff_rename_eq_zero` and `constantCoeff_rename` (or from a `coeff_toMvPowerSeries` formula).

batch3/probe1.lean (P1, P1b) and batch3/modified.lean: under `variable {R σ : Type*} [CommSemiring R]`:
example {f : R⟦X⟧} {i : σ} {d : σ →₀ ℕ} (hd : d i = 0) (hf : f.constantCoeff = 0) :
    (f.toMvPowerSeries i).coeff d = 0 := by
  rcases eq_or_ne d 0 with rfl | h0
  · rw [toMvPowerSeries_apply, MvPowerSeries.coeff_zero_eq_constantCoeff_apply,
      MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff_rename]
    exact hf
  · refine MvPowerSeries.coeff_rename_eq_zero _ _ ?_
    rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
    apply h0
    rw [Finsupp.unique_single x, Finsupp.mapDomain_single] at hd ⊢
    simp_all

findings.claim: Several docstrings still describe the pre-`ValueGroup₀` design. The field `RankLeOne.hom'` and the abbrev `RankOne.hom` say 'The inclusion morphism from `Γ₀` to `ℝ≥0`', and `RankOne`'s docstring says 'an inclusion morphism `Γ₀ → ℝ≥0`', but the map is `v.ValueGroup₀ →*₀ ℝ≥0`. findings.claim: The module, `RankLeOne` and `RankOne` docstrings call `v.ValueGroup₀` the valuation's 'image', but it is the group generated by the nonzero values, with zero adjoined. findings.claim: The class tower MonadWhiskerRight → MonadHorizontalComp → MonadWhiskerLeft → MonadNormalExpr is fully determined by `MonadMor₂`: both instances in Mathlib (Monoidal/Normalize.lean L777-787, Bicategory/Normalize.lean L538-548) are the same generic code, differing only in `hConsM`, where the bicategory version throws (and `MonadMor₂.horizontalCompM` for bicategories throws too). A generic `[Monad m] [MonadMor₂ m] : MonadNormalExpr m` is `rfl`-equal to the monoidal instance and agrees field by field with the bicategory one on nilM/consM/whiskerLeftM/whiskerRightM. The three parent classes are never used as an instance argument anywhere in Mathlib (only `MonadNormalExpr` is, at Normalize.lean L207/L355/L514 and Coherence/Basic.lean L42/L98). The linear `extends` chain also makes `MonadWhiskerLeft` require `hConsM`, which bicategories cannot supply.
findings.fix: Replace the four classes by plain `def`s (or one generic instance) over `[MonadMor₂ m]`, and delete the duplicated instance bodies in Monoidal/Normalize.lean and Bicategory/Normalize.lean.
findings.ev: hunts/coherence-normalize/batch1/Probe1.lean section C: `abbrev genericNormalExpr {m} [Monad m] [MonadMor₂ m] : MonadNormalExpr m where whiskerRightM η h := do return .whisker (← MonadMor₂.whiskerRightM η.e (.of h)) η h; hConsM η θ := do return .cons (← MonadMor₂.horizontalCompM η.e θ.e) η θ; whiskerLeftM f η := do return .whisker (← MonadMor₂.whiskerLeftM (.of f) η.e) f η; nilM α := do return .nil (← MonadMor₂.homM α) α; consM α η ηs := do return .cons (← MonadMor₂.comp₂M (← MonadMor₂.homM α) (← MonadMor₂.comp₂M η.e ηs.e)) α η ηs` then `example : (genericNormalExpr : MonadNormalExpr Monoidal.MonoidalM) = (inferInstance : MonadNormalExpr Monoidal.MonoidalM) := rfl` and the field-wise `rfl`s for Bicategory.BicategoryM (nilM, consM, whiskerLeftM, whiskerRightM) all compile; `git grep -nw MonadWhiskerLeft origin/master -- Mathlib MathlibTest` shows no binder use.

findings.claim: In the `.of η, .whisker _ f θ` branch (line 481) the call `mkEvalHorizontalCompAux'OfWhisker f η θ ηθ η₁ ηθ₁ ηθ₂ e_η₁ e_ηθ …` passes `ηθ η₁` into the two NormalExpr slots that the class field (line 324) and its only implementation (Monoidal/Normalize.lean:549) read as `η₁ ηθ`, while the proofs are passed in the order the implementation expects. The Monoidal instance therefore builds `evalHorizontalCompAux'_of_whisker` with `η₁ :=` the normal form of `(η ▷ f) ⊗ θ` and `ηθ :=` the normal form of `η ▷ f`, which is ill-typed. `monoidal` then fails with '(kernel) application type mismatch' on every goal whose normalization reaches `η ⊗ₘ (X ◁ θ)`, even the reflexive `f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ g) = f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ g)`, and also on `(U ◁ f) ⊗ₘ (V ◁ g)`, `f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ V ◁ g)` and `𝟙_ C ◁ (f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ g))`. The kernel rejects the term, so nothing unsound is proved, but this branch of the evaluator returns a wrong certificate (and `eval`, `evalHorizontalComp` and the string-diagram widget inherit it). All 26 other reflexive branch probes pass. With the two arguments swapped, every failing goal closes, including the non-reflexive `f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ g) = (α_ _ _ _).inv ≫ ((f ▷ U) ⊗ₘ g) ≫ (α_ _ _ _).hom` (true by `simp [tensorHom_def]`). An open upstream PR, leanprover-community/mathlib4#44543 (opened 2026-10-06, unmerged at 4beb549110), makes exactly this fix. Graded MAJOR, not CRITICAL: the kernel rejects the ill-typed certificate, so nothing false is proved; the tactic fails on true goals in its domain (reproduced independently: `example : f ⊗ₘ (Z ◁ g) = f ⊗ₘ (Z ◁ g) := by monoidal` → (kernel) application type mismatch, while `(X ◁ f) ⊗ₘ g` works). Found independently by batches 0–3 and by Astra's blind pass (its top finding), but ALREADY FIXED UPSTREAM by open PR leanprover-community/mathlib4#44543 (gaetanserre, opened 2026-10-06, identical one-line swap plus tests) — not our discovery; no draft PR opened.
findings.fix: Pass `η₁ ηθ` instead of `ηθ η₁` at line 481 and rename the class binders to `e_η₁ e_ηθ`, as upstream PR #44543 does; add the reflexive regression tests.

import Mathlib.Tactic.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Basic
open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y Z W U : C}
example (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ W) : f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ g) = f ⊗ₘ (U ◁ g) := by monoidal
-- error: (kernel) application type mismatch  @Monoidal.evalHorizontalCompAux'_of_whisker C _ _ U Z X W Y f g (…tensorHom (whiskerRight f U) g…)
--   argument has type (X ⊗ U) ⊗ Z ⟶ (Y ⊗ U) ⊗ W but function has type ∀ {η₁ : X ⊗ U ⟶ Y ⊗ U} …
-- Full probes: hunts/coherence-normalize/batch3/P1.lean (T1c, line 32; T2g, line 63) and hunts/coherence-normalize/batch3/P2.lean section R (R11/R17/R21/R22, lines 133/142/147/148: kernel errors; the 26 other reflexive branch goals pass). Fix check: P2.lean section F1 (`monoidal_fixHC`, the shipped instance with the two NormalExpr arguments swapped, i.e. the call-site fix) closes all of them with no errors. | main/repro.lean: `by monoidal` on `f ⊗ₘ (Z ◁ g) = f ⊗ₘ (Z ◁ g)` → (kernel) application type mismatch.
findings.astraS: Astra's blind A1 pass independently ranked this its top (P1 correctness) finding: the `.of η, .whisker _ f θ` branch passes `ηθ η₁` where the interface and monoidal builder expect `η₁ ηθ`, producing a kernel-rejected proof; fix by swapping (plus renaming the class's `e_` binders).

findings.claim: In the `.isoHom`/`.isoInv` branches, `eval` accepts only a structural *atom* or an atomic iso; any other iso goes to `| _ => throwError "not implemented. try dsimp first."` (lines 534, 542). So `monoidal` fails on purely structural goals that its docstring covers and `monoidal_coherence` proves: `(α_ X Y Z ≪≫ (α_ X Y Z).symm).hom = 𝟙 _`, `(α_ X Y Z).symm.hom = (α_ X Y Z).inv`, `(whiskerLeftIso W (α_ X Y Z)).hom = W ◁ (α_ X Y Z).hom`. `bicategory` fails in the same way. `eval` also rejects its own output: normal forms are built from `(… ≪≫ …).hom` and `(whiskerLeftIso …).hom` structural composites, so `monoidal_nf` followed by `monoidal` fails even on `f ≫ g = f ≫ g`. The docstring ('Evaluate the expression of a 2-morphism into a normalized form') does not mention the restriction. The `isStructural` predicate defined at line 111, unused anywhere in Mathlib, is exactly what this case needs. Non-structural composites such as `(α ≪≫ β).hom` also fail. That case is outside this fix, and the error message points to the `dsimp` workaround. Graded MINOR, not MAJOR: the branch throws an explicit "not implemented. try dsimp first." — a signposted limitation, not a wrong result. Reproduced: `monoidal` on `(α_ X Y Z).symm.hom = (α_ X Y Z).inv` and `monoidal_nf; monoidal` on `f ≫ g = f ≫ g` both fail with that message (main/repro2.lean); `monoidal_coherence` proves the first. No upstream report found.
findings.fix: Replace the `.structuralAtom α` cases by `| α => if α.isStructural then return ⟨← nilM α, ← mkEqRefl e.e⟩` (and `nilM (← symmM α)` for `isoInv`). This was checked: it closes the three structural goals, the `monoidal_nf; monoidal` re-entry and the bicategory analogue, and leaves the existing `monoidal` tests passing.

import Mathlib.Tactic.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Basic
open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y Z W : C}

findings.claim: `isMVarSwap` ("`true` if `s` and `t` are equal up to swapping the `MVarId`s") ignores universe levels in its `.sort` and `.const` branches whenever the expression has level parameters, so it identifies expressions that differ in rigid universes: `isMVarSwap (.sort (.param u)) (.sort (.succ (.param u)))` and `isMVarSwap (.const ULift [u+1, 0]) (.const ULift [u, 0])` both return `true`. Since a `true` result makes `Entries.addConst`/`addFVar` drop the reverse (`←`) rewrite entry, such lemmas lose their reverse rewrite suggestion. The pruning also ignores premises: for `h : ∀ a b, a ≤ b → f a b = f b a` the reverse entry is dropped although `← h a b hab` is the useful direction.
findings.fix: Compare universe levels (up to level-metavariable renaming) in the `.sort`/`.const` branches, and only prune the reverse entry when the premises are also symmetric.

findings.claim: `evalAbs` matches `@abs _ $instLattice $instAddGroup $a`, synthesizes its own `Ring`/`IsOrderedRing`, and uses `assumeInstancesCommute` without checking that these agree with the captured `AddGroup`. With a non-canonical `AddGroup ℚ` (transferred along `x ↦ x - 1`, so zero is `1` and `|0| = 2`), `norm_num` reduces the *true* goal `|0| = 2` to `⊢ False`, and on `|0| = 0` it produces a certificate the kernel rejects ('application type mismatch'). Nothing unsound follows, since the kernel catches it, but the tactic misleads. The unchecked `assumeInstancesCommute` pattern is common in norm_num extensions. Graded MINOR: tactic robustness on non-canonical instances, not a wrong library statement.
findings.fix: Use `assertInstancesCommute` (or check the captured instances against the synthesized ones) and fail gracefully on mismatch.
findings.ev: -- hunts/normnum-abs/P2.lean: `abbrev shiftedAddGroup : AddGroup ℚ := shift.addGroup` (shift x = x - 1); `example : @abs ℚ inferInstance shiftedAddGroup 0 = 2 := by norm_num` → `unsolved goals ⊢ False` plus a (kernel) application type mismatch; `... = 0 := by norm_num` → (kernel) application type mismatch on `isNat_eq_true (isNat_abs_nonneg ...)`.

findings.claim: The module docstring and `LightDiagram`'s docstring never say that morphisms of `LightDiagram` are all continuous maps between the limit spaces (the category is induced from `Profinite` via `toProfinite`), not maps of the chosen towers; e.g. the identity of the two-point space is a morphism from the tower `pt, 2, 2, …` to the constant tower `2`, though no natural transformation of towers induces it. Readers of 'the equivalence `LightProfinite ≌ LightDiagram`' can easily misread what it asserts (Astra A1 item 11).
findings.fix: State in the docstrings that `LightDiagram` is a full subcategory-like category of `Profinite` (morphisms are continuous maps of the limits).

findings.claim: `@[simps!]` on the `Category LightDiagram` instance generates only the fully applied `LightDiagram.id_hom_hom_hom_apply` and `LightDiagram.comp_hom_hom_hom_apply`, whose right-hand side uses the raw field `TopCat.Hom.hom'`. Nothing in the file uses them: the file compiles with `@[simps!]` deleted (CopyA). The standard induced-category API that `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` (`hom_ext`, `FullSubcategory.id_hom`, `FullSubcategory.comp_hom`) and `CommMon` provide is missing. As a result `simp` makes no progress on `(f ≫ g).hom = f.hom ≫ g.hom` or on `InducedCategory.Hom.hom (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 X.toProfinite`, although both hold by `rfl`. It also fails on `lightDiagramToProfinite.map (f ≫ g) = f.hom ≫ g.hom`, leaving `(f ≫ g).hom = f.hom ≫ g.hom`. With the generated lemma, `simp` leaves `g.hom.hom.hom' (f.hom.hom.hom' a) = (TopCat.Hom.hom g.hom.hom) ((TopCat.Hom.hom f.hom.hom) a)`. The same goal in a FullSubcategory (control) is closed by `simp`. Adding `id_hom`, `comp_hom` and `hom_ext` (CopyE) makes `simp` and `ext` close all of these goals.
findings.fix: Replace `@[simps!]` by explicit `@[simp] id_hom`, `@[simp, reassoc] comp_hom` and `@[ext] hom_ext` lemmas at the `InducedCategory.Hom` level, as `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` does.
